text.p: Australia revived their Tri-Nations challenge and lifted the spirits of troubled coach Greg Smith with a 32-20 win over South Africa on Saturday.
The Wallabies bounced back from their opening defeat by competition leaders and holders New Zealand last weekend by running in four tries to three at Brisbane's Suncorp Stadium.
It was the highest score by an Australian side in a test against South Africa.
After two heavy defeats by the All Blacks last month, Smith acknowledged his team's performance against South Africa could determine whether he retained control next year.
Winger Ben Tune crossed twice for tries and fullback Stephen Larkham and number eight Daniel Manu also went over to give the home side a decisive 26-10 lead at halftime.
Flyhalf David Knox, who revitalised Australia's backline on his recall in place of the injured Tim Horan, kicked three conversions and two penalties to cap a fine return.
South Africa replied with tries from prop Os du Randt and late scores by lock Mark Andrews and flyhalf Jannie de Beer. De Beer added one penalty and a conversion.
